description: A diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that preserves the DiagnosisProbe interface while supporting changes to the recommendation model. Diagnostics use only observed interaction histories, item titles, descriptions, timestamps, and model behavior.
motivation: Keep model diagnosis compatible with the shared RecHarness benchmark, prevent unsupported claims about unavailable user traits or item attributes, and select models using comparable validation results.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the trained nn.Module through view.model and preserve or adapt the item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility interfaces. Batches contain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. Treat unavailable review data and simulator traits as unobserved. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Preserve all four dataset routes and select models by macro-average validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Any architecture change must also update the predictor writer.
pseudocode:
initialize DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    preserve model training mode; enter evaluation mode with gradients disabled
    inspect permitted histories and available metadata
    compute applicable representation and prediction diagnostics from batches
    generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five training users per category
    report measured diagnostics with definitions, sample counts, and unavailable-data status
    restore model training mode
    return metrics, metric_definitions
Externally select trials using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines architecture-compatible diagnostics with explicit data-availability constraints.
originality.negative: Primarily an integration contract rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can support consistent diagnosis across evolving architectures and guide validation-tested changes.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic usefulness and recommendation gains require empirical validation; latent simulator traits cannot be established from the available data.

code_difficulty.positive: The fixed interface and batch format provide a clear implementation boundary.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture adaptation, full-catalog scoring, and synchronization with the generated predictor require careful implementation.
